akhfash:7-9.t:
He said ﴿فَعَدَلَكَ﴾, that is: thus He created you; and some read it light. Whoever reads it heavy, ﴿عَدَّلَك﴾, is only saying "He proportioned your form" (عَدَّلَ خَلْقَكَ); and "عَدَلَكَ" means: He balanced parts of you against other parts of you and made you even and well-proportioned, and it is in the meaning of "عدّلك".
And He said ﴿خَلَقَكَ﴾ and ﴿رَكَّبَكَ﴾ ﴿كَلاَّ﴾; and if you wish, you say ﴿خَلَقَك﴾ and ﴿رَكَّبَكْ﴾ ﴿كَلاَّ﴾ with assimilation (idghām), because they are two identical letters, and of two identical letters one is assimilated into its companion. And if you wish, when both are vowelled, you make the first quiescent and vowel the second. When the first is quiescent there is no assimilation, and when the first is vowelled and the second quiescent there is no assimilation. «[Translator's note: so in the source; one would expect "when the first is quiescent there is nothing but assimilation".]»

akhfash:19-19.t: And He said ﴿يَوْمَ لاَ تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ﴾: He made "the day" (mean) a time (ḥīn), as if, when He said ﴿وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ﴾, He said "at a time when no soul has power" (في حين لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ). And some read ﴿يَوْمُ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ﴾, making it an explanation of the first "day", as if He said: "it is a day when (no soul) has power" (هُوَ يوم لا تملك).

daas-irab:1-5.t: The i'rab of verses like these has already been given in Sūrat al-Takwīr.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿يا﴾: a vocative particle; ﴿أَيُّهَا﴾: the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; ﴿ها﴾: a particle drawing attention (tanbīh); ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾: badal (substitute); ﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿غَرَّكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of ما; ﴿بِرَبِّكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْكَرِيمِ﴾: naʿt (adjective).

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a second naʿt (adjective) of ربك; ﴿خَلَقَكَ﴾: a past verb and its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿فَسَوَّاكَ﴾: conjoined to خلقك; ﴿فَعَدَلَكَ﴾: also conjoined.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿فِي أَيِّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ركبك; ﴿صُورَةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿ما﴾: redundant (zāʾida); ﴿شاءَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of صورة; ﴿رَكَّبَكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿بَلْ﴾: a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī); ﴿تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بِالدِّينِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and inna is a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters); ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿لَحافِظِينَ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿حافظين﴾ is the postponed noun of inna; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿ما﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿تَفْعَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْأَبْرارَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿لَفِي﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿في نَعِيمٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:14-14.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿يَصْلَوْنَها﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿يَوْمَ الدِّينِ﴾: an adverb of time, muḍāf to الدين.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and ﴿ما﴾ is Ḥijāzī, working like laysa; ﴿هُمْ﴾: its noun; ﴿عَنْها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows; ﴿بِغائِبِينَ﴾: genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of ما; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle and ﴿ما﴾ is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَدْراكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of ما, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿ما يَوْمُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿الدِّينِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause stands in place of the second object of أدراك.

daas-irab:18-18.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is the same.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb; ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿لِنَفْسٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿شَيْئاً﴾: direct object; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَالْأَمْرُ﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle and ﴿الْأَمْرُ﴾ is mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time annexed to one like it, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾: attached to the omitted khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive.

farraa:1-1.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنفَطَرَتْ﴾: it was split.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ﴾.
What is in its belly of gold and silver came out, and the dead came out after that. It is one of the portents of the Hour that the earth brings out the pieces of its liver (أفلاذ كبدها), of its gold and its silver. Al-Farrāʾ said: الأفلاذ are pieces of liver cut lengthwise, المشرّح and المشرّحة; the singular is فِلْذ and فِلْذة.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ﴾ of its deeds ﴿وَأَخَّرَتْ﴾.
And what it left behind: whatever practice (sunna), good or evil, it established which was then acted upon.
The response (jawāb) to ﴿إذا السَّماء انفطَرتْ﴾ (1) is His saying: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ﴾.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read it: "فَعَدَلَك", lightened, and the people of the Hijaz read it: "فعدَّلك", with shadda. Whoever reads it lightened, its interpretation — and Allah knows best — is: He turned you into whatever form He willed: either handsome or ugly, or tall or short.
He said: [al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying]: One of the shaykhs narrated to me from Layth from Ibn Abī Najīḥ that he said: in the form of a paternal uncle, in the form of a father, in the form of one of the relatives, by resemblance.
Whoever reads "فعدَّلك" with shadda means — and Allah knows best —: He made you well-proportioned, of balanced make. That is the more pleasing of the two to me and the better of them in Arabic, because you say: ﴿فى أى صورة ما شاء ركبك﴾ (in whatever form He willed He assembled you), so making في belong to the assembling (التركيب) is stronger in Arabic than making في belong to العدل (turning); [130/b] because saying عدلتك إلى كذا وكذا (I turned you to such and such) and صرفتك إلى كذا وكذا is better than saying عدلتك فيه and صرفتك فيه.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كَلاَّ بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِٱلدِّينِ﴾.
With tāʾ. Some of the people of Medina read it with yāʾ, and some of them with tāʾ; al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim with tāʾ. The tāʾ is the better of the two because of His saying: "وإِنَّ عَلَيكُم" — He did not say: عليهم.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَا هُمْ عَنْهَا بِغَآئِبِينَ﴾.
He says: once they enter it, they will not be brought out of it. The readers agreed on the accusative in ﴿يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ﴾ (19), and the nominative would be permissible if it were read so. Al-Kisāʾī claimed that the Arabs prefer the nominative when they annex اليوم to يفعل, تفعل, أفعل and نفعل, saying: هذا يومُ نفعلُ ذاك (this is the day we do that), and أفعل ذاك, and نفعل ذاك. But when they say هذا يومَ فعلتَ, annexing يوم to فعلتُ or to إذ, they prefer the accusative. They recited to us:
عَلى حينَ عاتبْتُ المشيبَ على الصِّبا * وقُلتُ أَلَمَّا تَصْحُ والشَّيبُ وازِعُ؟
(At the time when I reproached grey hair for [the loss of] youth, and said: Have you not yet sobered up, when grey hair is a restrainer?)
With the yāʾ and tāʾ [forms] what is permissible with فعلت is also permissible; but most common is what al-Kisāʾī explained.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Infiṭār
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إذا السَّماءُ انْفَطَرَتْ﴾, that is: "split open". The heaven will split open on the Day of Resurrection with the clouds, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said.
«[Translator's note: the source quotes no verse after "as He said".]»

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَإذا الكَواكِبُ انْتَثَرَتْ﴾, that is: they fell down and dropped one after another.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَإذا البِحارُ فُجِّرَتْ﴾: the sweet water burst forth into the salt.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿وَإذا القُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ﴾: he means «بُحْثِرَتْ», that is: their earth is turned over and the dead in them are resurrected.

zajjaj:5-5.t: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ وأخَّرَتْ﴾: what it sent ahead of the deeds it was commanded to do, and what it held back of them and did not do. It was also said: «وَأخَّرَتْ» means: whatever practice (sunna) it instituted that was acted upon after it.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الإنْسانُ ما غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الكَرِيمِ﴾, that is: what deceived you and enticed you until you neglected what was obligatory upon you?!

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ﴾, that is: He created you in the best stature. It is read «فَعَدَّلَكَ» both without doubling and with doubling.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿فِي أيِّ صُورَةٍ ما شاءَ رَكَّبَكَ﴾: «ما» may be an emphasising connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant), and the meaning is: "in whatever form He willed He assembled you — whether tall or short, whether handsome or otherwise." And «ما» may be in the sense of condition and requital (sharṭ wa-jazāʾ), so that the meaning is: "in whatever form He wills to assemble you in, He assembles you."

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿كَلا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِ﴾, that is: rather, you deny that you will be resurrected and judged, that is, requited for your deeds. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, informed them that their deeds are preserved, saying: ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ ما تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 12], so they write it down against them.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿يَصْلَوْنَها يَوْمَ الدِّينِ﴾: the Day of Requital, which is the Day of Resurrection.

zajjaj:17-18.t: His saying: ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما يَوْمُ الدِّينِ﴾ ﴿ثُمَّ ما أدْراكَ ما يَوْمُ الدِّينِ﴾: He repeated the mention of the day to magnify its importance.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾ — it was also read «يَوْمُ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ». Whoever read it in the nominative did so on the basis that the "day" is an attribute (ṣifa) of His saying «يَوْمُ الدِّينِ». It may also be nominative with «هُوَ» implied, so that the meaning is: "it is a day when no soul will have power to do anything for another soul." It may also be in the position of the nominative while being indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, because it is annexed to His saying «لا تَمْلِكُ»; for what is annexed to something not fully declinable (ghayr al-mutamakkin) may be made indeclinable on the fatḥa, even though it is in the position of a nominative or a genitive, as the poet said:
؎لَمْ يَمْنَعِ الشُّرْبَ مِنها غَيْرَ أنْ نَطَقَتْ ∗∗∗ حَمامَةٌ في غُصُونٍ ذاتِ أوْقالِ
(Nothing kept her from drinking except that a dove cooed among branches laden with fruit.)
— he annexed «غَيْرَ» to «أنْ نَطَقَتْ» and so made it indeclinable on the fatḥa. And its accusative may be according to the meaning of these things mentioned: it is ﴿يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾.
«[Translator's note: the source text ends here; the explanation of the accusative appears to be incomplete.]»
